landmarks.explanation: Burj Khalifa in Dubai has been the world's tallest building since it opened in 2010, at about 828 metres.
Stonehenge is a prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire, England, built in stages from around 3000 BC.
El Castillo, the stepped pyramid of Kukulcán, stands at the centre of the Maya city of Chichén Itzá in Yucatán, Mexico.
Tower Bridge crosses the River Thames in London and opened in 1894; its roadway lifts to let ships through.
The glass pyramid designed by I. M. Pei became the main entrance of the Louvre museum in Paris in 1989.
Napoleon commissioned the Arc de Triomphe in Paris in 1806; it was completed in 1836.
Berlin's neoclassical Brandenburg Gate was completed in 1791 and became a symbol of German reunification.
Notre-Dame stands on the Île de la Cité in Paris; it reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire.

options: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
landmarks.explanation: Saint Basil's Cathedral, with its colourful onion domes, was built on Red Square in Moscow in the 1550s under Ivan the Terrible.
Hagia Sophia in Istanbul was completed in 537 as the cathedral of Constantinople, and its great dome still dominates the skyline.
The Sultan Ahmed Mosque in Istanbul, completed in 1616, is called the Blue Mosque after the blue tiles inside.
Mont-Saint-Michel is a tidal island in Normandy, France, crowned by a medieval abbey.
Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain at 3,776 metres and an active volcano.
The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon in Arizona, USA, over millions of years.
Niagara Falls lies on the border between Ontario, Canada, and New York, USA.
Uluru is a huge sandstone rock in Australia's Northern Territory, sacred to the Aṉangu people.
Flat-topped Table Mountain overlooks the city of Cape Town in South Africa.
Ha Long Bay in Vietnam is dotted with thousands of limestone islands and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Victoria Falls is on the Zambezi River, on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
The pyramid-shaped Matterhorn rises 4,478 metres on the border between Switzerland and Italy.
The White Tower at the heart of the Tower of London was begun by William the Conqueror around 1078.
Buckingham Palace in London is the official London residence of the British monarch.
Louis XIV moved the French royal court to the Palace of Versailles in 1682.
Edinburgh Castle sits on Castle Rock, the plug of an ancient volcano, above Scotland's capital.
Building of Prague's Charles Bridge over the Vltava began in 1357; it is lined with 30 statues.
Florence's Ponte Vecchio crosses the Arno and is still lined with shops, mostly jewellers.
The stone Rialto Bridge over Venice's Grand Canal was completed in 1591.

options: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
landmarks.explanation: St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City has a dome designed by Michelangelo.
Filippo Brunelleschi's dome on Florence Cathedral was completed in 1436 and is still the largest brick dome ever built.
Milan Cathedral took nearly six centuries to complete and is covered in spires and statues.
Cologne Cathedral's twin Gothic spires rise 157 metres; it was finally completed in 1880.
The Atomium in Brussels was built for Expo 58 and models an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.
The Alhambra in Granada, Spain, was the palace-fortress of the Nasrid rulers.
The Potala Palace in Lhasa, Tibet, was the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas.
At Beijing's Temple of Heaven, emperors prayed for good harvests; the round hall dates from the Ming dynasty.
landmarks.photoQuery: Temple of Heaven Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests

landmarks.explanation: Thousands of clay soldiers were buried with China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, and found near Xi'an in 1974.
Fushimi Inari Taisha in Kyoto is famous for paths lined with thousands of vermilion torii gates.
Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion in Kyoto, is covered in gold leaf; it was rebuilt in 1955 after a fire.
Himeji Castle is nicknamed the White Heron Castle for its brilliant white walls.
Kuala Lumpur's Petronas Towers, finished in 1998, are the tallest twin towers in the world, linked by a skybridge.
Marina Bay Sands in Singapore opened in 2010; a sky park sits across the tops of its three towers.
Dubai's sail-shaped Burj Al Arab hotel stands on an artificial island and opened in 1999.
The white marble Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi was completed in 2007.
The Gateway of India on Mumbai's waterfront was completed in 1924.
India Gate in New Delhi is a war memorial to Indian soldiers who died in the First World War.
The Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar is the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism.
Jaipur's pink sandstone Hawa Mahal, built in 1799, has 953 small windows.
New Delhi's Lotus Temple is a Baháʼí House of Worship shaped like a lotus flower; it opened in 1986.
Delhi's Qutub Minar is a tapering brick minaret about 73 metres tall, begun around 1200.
The Charminar in Hyderabad, India, with its four minarets, was built in 1591.
The gilded Shwedagon Pagoda towers over Yangon and is Myanmar's most sacred Buddhist site.
Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, stands on the bank of the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok.
Borobudur in Central Java, Indonesia, is a 9th-century temple and the largest Buddhist temple in the world.
More than 2,000 Buddhist temples and pagodas still stand on the plain of Bagan in Myanmar.
Abu Simbel's giant statues of Ramesses II were moved to higher ground in the 1960s to escape the Aswan Dam's lake.
The Great Sphinx of Giza, a lion with a human head, was carved from limestone in ancient Egypt.
Casablanca's Hassan II Mosque stands on the Atlantic shore and has a minaret about 210 metres tall.
Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is Africa's highest mountain at 5,895 metres.
Toronto's CN Tower, completed in 1976, is 553 metres tall.
Seattle's Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair.
New York's Empire State Building was completed in 1931 and was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.
The Art Deco Chrysler Building in New York, with its stainless-steel crown, was completed in 1930.
New York's triangular Flatiron Building was completed in 1902.
The White House in Washington, D.C., has been home to every US president since John Adams in 1800.
The domed United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., is the seat of the US Congress.
The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., opened in 1922 with a giant seated statue of Abraham Lincoln.
St. Louis's stainless-steel Gateway Arch, completed in 1965, is 192 metres tall, the tallest arch in the world.
The Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883, linking Manhattan and Brooklyn across the East River.
Budapest's Hungarian Parliament Building on the Danube was completed in 1904.
Berlin's Reichstag building got its glass dome, designed by Norman Foster, in 1999.
Seville's Plaza de España was built for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929.
The colourful Pena Palace sits on a hilltop above Sintra, Portugal.
Lisbon's Belém Tower is a 16th-century fortification on the Tagus River.
Rome's Baroque Trevi Fountain was completed in 1762; visitors toss coins into it.
Rome's Pantheon, finished around AD 125, still has the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.
At Meteora in Greece, monasteries sit on top of tall rock pillars.
The Cliffs of Moher in County Clare, Ireland, rise up to 214 metres above the Atlantic.
About 40,000 interlocking basalt columns form the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland.
The Twelve Apostles are limestone sea stacks along the Great Ocean Road in Victoria, Australia.
Sugarloaf Mountain rises 396 metres above Guanabara Bay in Rio de Janeiro; a cable car runs to the top.

cuisines.explanation: Fish and chips, battered fried fish with thick-cut chips, became a popular takeaway in England in the 1800s.
A hamburger is a cooked patty of ground meat served in a sliced bun, usually with toppings.
Jollof rice is cooked in a tomato, onion and pepper sauce and is loved across West Africa.
Carbonara is a Roman pasta dish made with egg, hard cheese, cured pork and black pepper.
Lasagna layers wide flat pasta sheets with sauce and cheese and is baked in the oven.
Risotto is a northern Italian rice dish cooked slowly in broth until creamy.
Tabbouleh is a Levantine salad of finely chopped parsley, tomato, mint and bulgur.
The pretzel, a bread knotted into a distinctive shape, has long been a speciality of southern Germany.
A bagel is a ring of dough that is boiled briefly and then baked.
Wiener schnitzel is a thin, breaded and fried veal cutlet from Vienna, Austria.
Shawarma is meat roasted on a vertical spit, shaved thin and often wrapped in flatbread.
Crêpes are very thin pancakes from France, served sweet or savoury.
French macarons are almond-meringue cookies sandwiched with a filling.
Ratatouille is a stewed vegetable dish from Provence, France, made with tomato, aubergine, courgette and peppers.
Bouillabaisse is a fish stew from the port city of Marseille, France.
A croque monsieur is a French toasted ham-and-cheese sandwich, often topped with béchamel.
A Greek salad combines tomato, cucumber, onion, olives and a slab of feta cheese.
Gazpacho is a cold tomato-based soup from Andalusia in southern Spain.
Bunny chow, a hollowed-out loaf of bread filled with curry, comes from Durban, South Africa.
A full breakfast typically includes eggs, bacon, sausages, beans, tomatoes and toast.
Eggs Benedict is poached egg and ham on an English muffin, topped with hollandaise sauce.
American-style pancakes are thick and fluffy and often stacked with butter and syrup.
Waffles are cooked between patterned hot plates, which gives them their grid of pockets.
Apple pie is a pastry-crust pie filled with spiced apple.
Cheesecake has a creamy layer of soft cheese on a base of crushed biscuit or pastry.
Macaroni and cheese is pasta baked or stirred in a cheese sauce.
New England clam chowder is a creamy soup of clams and potatoes.
Knafeh is a Middle Eastern dessert of shredded pastry or semolina over soft cheese, soaked in syrup.
A burrito is a large flour tortilla wrapped around fillings such as rice, beans and meat.
Guacamole is a Mexican dip of mashed avocado with lime, onion and chilli.
Tamales are masa dough steamed in a corn husk or banana leaf, a staple across Mexico and Central America.
Enchiladas are rolled corn tortillas filled and covered in chilli sauce.
Feijoada, a black bean stew with pork, is often called Brazil's national dish.
Pão de queijo are small Brazilian cheese breads made with cassava flour.
Brigadeiros are Brazilian chocolate sweets rolled in chocolate sprinkles.
Chili con carne is a spicy stew of chilli peppers and meat, often with beans, associated with Texas.
Naan is a leavened flatbread traditionally baked against the wall of a tandoor oven.
Tandoori chicken is marinated in yoghurt and spices and roasted in a tandoor, which gives it its red colour and char.
Chole bhature pairs spicy chickpea curry with puffy deep-fried bread, a favourite in North India.
Pav bhaji, a spiced mashed-vegetable curry with buttered bread rolls, is a Mumbai street food.
Gulab jamun are fried milk-dough balls soaked in a fragrant sugar syrup.
Idli are steamed cakes of fermented rice and lentil batter from South India.
Jalebi are spirals of fried batter soaked in syrup, popular across South Asia and the Middle East.
Laksa is a spicy noodle soup, often with coconut curry broth, from Malaysia and Singapore.
Nasi lemak is rice cooked in coconut milk, served with sambal, anchovies, peanuts and egg; it is Malaysia's national dish.
Nasi goreng is Indonesian fried rice, often topped with a fried egg.
Satay is skewered grilled meat served with peanut sauce, popular in Indonesia and Malaysia.
Rendang is beef slow-cooked in coconut milk and spices until almost dry, from Indonesia's Minangkabau people.
Tom yum is a hot and sour Thai soup flavoured with lemongrass, lime leaves and chilli.
Thai green curry gets its colour from green chillies in the curry paste, cooked with coconut milk.
Spring rolls are thin pastry wrappers rolled around a filling and usually fried.
Xiaolongbao are soup dumplings from Shanghai, steamed in bamboo baskets.
Mapo tofu is a Sichuan dish of tofu in a spicy, numbing chilli and bean sauce.
At a Chinese hot pot, diners cook raw ingredients at the table in a simmering pot of broth.
Kimchi is Korean fermented cabbage, usually seasoned with chilli, garlic and ginger.
Tteokbokki are chewy Korean rice cakes in a sweet and spicy red chilli sauce.
Tempura is seafood or vegetables fried in a very light, crisp batter, a classic of Japanese cooking.
Takoyaki are batter balls filled with octopus, cooked in a special moulded pan in Osaka, Japan.
Mochi is a Japanese rice cake made from pounded glutinous rice.
Pastéis de nata are Portuguese custard tarts with crisp, flaky pastry and a caramelised top.
